low_level: Registers 40 to 255 over the 383 distinct kernels behind the card's cells (52 with register spills, a kernel measured in more than one batch counts once), shared memory 672 to 22528 bytes, harness 0.10 on umbriel-b200-047, umbriel-b200-068.
Adapter statics: input arrangement striped, output indices, temp storage 640 to 2304 bytes.

Oracle battery (23 cases per cell plus the measurement seeds) passed on every cell that has a number, 145 cells unsupported by the adapter's contract or the device, 6 cells failed the oracle and carry no number.
Phase 3b sorted-output check (umbriel-b200-047): 60 cells passed the order check, 6 cells failed it (see the negative findings).
algorithmic: Random input (the one-node matrix on umbriel-b200-047): latency not_guaranteed wins 21 of 60 cells (runner-up in 23), latency prefer_smaller_index wins 20 of 50 cells (runner-up in 17), throughput not_guaranteed wins 34 of 59 cells (runner-up in 8), throughput prefer_smaller_index wins 30 of 50 cells (runner-up in 6).

Where it wins on random input (bf16 N 512, bf16 N 1024, bf16 N 2048, bf16 N 4096, fp32 N 512, fp32 N 1024, fp32 N 2048, fp32 N 4096), the median margin over the runner-up is +45 percent and over the scope's reference control +1068 percent.

Largest random-input deficits (distinct cells, worst regime): fp32 N 256 k 64 +216 percent behind N6w_atom32 in latency prefer_smaller_index, bf16 N 256 k 64 +186 percent behind N5_rows_f in throughput not_guaranteed, fp32 N 256 k 48 +141 percent behind N6w_atom32 in latency prefer_smaller_index, bf16 N 256 k 48 +130 percent behind N5_rows_f in throughput not_guaranteed.

Tie-heavy input (unshuffled, umbriel-b200-068): latency not_guaranteed wins 1 of 28 cells (runner-up in 7), latency prefer_smaller_index wins 1 of 25 cells (runner-up in 5), throughput not_guaranteed wins 3 of 28 cells (runner-up in 3), throughput prefer_smaller_index wins 1 of 25 cells (runner-up in 3).
Named workloads won on random input: moe_nemotron3_ultra_512_top22, nsa_blocks_128k, nsa_blocks_32k, peer_subkey_top16.
negative: Phase 3b (umbriel-b200-047): six fp32 prefer_smaller_index cells fail the harness sorted-order check, k 16 and 64 at N 512, 2048 and 4096, on the quantized_random and relu_quantized rows (the signed-zero and tie rows passed). The sorted finish leaves equal keys inside the top k in scatter position order because the tie rewrite fixes only the class at the k-th slot. The unsorted cells stand.
surprises: On tie-heavy input the threshold filter loses its edge: the warp throughput cells it wins on random input go to W2_packed_v3 and N6w_atom32 under tie_heavy.
open_questions: The fix is the tie rewrite generalized to every class run inside the top k, open is whether the sorted output then costs anything over the unsorted path.

GB200 pass on gb200-nvl4-ts2-99 (WINNERS_gb200.md): the warp and sub-warp winners agree on 359 of 376 common cells (365 of 376 when each cell is compared through the adapters both passes measured, as section 16 of the knowledge base does), the differences are named sub-warp lane-count cells, N 128 sub-warp throughput cells and warp ties within 5 percent, and in the block matrices the B1_idx against B1_det2 throughput ties fall either way. The GB200 k 64 cells at 128 threads run 3 to 15 percent slower than on B200 (hw-researcher, a generation property).
